scope: Two finite repeats of twelve consecutive official MCP SDK 2.3.1 client-generated overload, cancellation and recovery cycles against one checksum-verified unsigned experimental Debian 12 amd64 package installed in a disposable route-free fixture container. The server used a 64-FD soft limit, 128 MiB memory limit and 64-PID cap.
reproduce: Install pinned SDK with npm ci --prefix tools/mcp-sdk-probe --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund; set OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_DIR to that directory, OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE to the verified .deb, OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE_SHA256 to its digest, then run bash tools/netns_adversarial_probe.sh target/debug/outbound-guard-mcp twice.
checks: Each run required all 12 held fetches to reach the controlled HTTP fixture; each 8-request SDK tools/list burst completed; each ninth marked call returned MCP_INPUT_BUSY with no marked HTTP hit; all 12 AbortSignal cancellations closed fixture sockets; audit events alternated EGRESS_CANCELLED and EGRESS_ALLOWED; all 12 approved GET recoveries returned fixture-ok in one installed server process; package install/hash/version, removal/residue, and no remaining container/namespace passed.
sampling: In-container /proc server FD sampling requested 5 ms intervals during all 12 cycles; reported max is a sampled lower bound on transient peak. VmHWM is process-specific; container memory/PID high-water marks include helpers.
limitations: Finite single-client SDK session and one Debian artifact only. No sustained or arbitrary concurrency, other platform, Claude/Codex/Cursor-generated overload, traffic through other tools, exact official candidate, owner residual-risk acceptance or independent human review is claimed. The four AI Scraping Defense repositories require separate evidence. Initial development runs exposed a test-harness monitor timing error and incomplete expected audit sequence; a CI-only finish-handshake race was then found and fixed. All three harness errors were corrected before these two passing repeats.
